 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH  ORAL ORDER 7 10-04-2019 Learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the the State have assisted the Court.
2. The petitioner has moved the Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Code') for the following relief:
"That this is an application for quashing the order dated 06.02.2014 passed by the Court of Sub- Divisional Magistrate, Purnea in Complaint Case No. B-III-19/11 registered under Sections 16(1)A of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as "PFA Act") for reasons of violation of Section 2(ix) (j) and (k) of PFA Act read with Rule 32(b)(2)(iv) and Rule 32A and 37A of the PFA Rules,
1955-refusing to discharge the petitioner on grounds that are non est in the eyes of law and is based on wrong appreciation of the facts and law."

sentences.text: After hearing the petitioner for some time and going through the materials on record, the Court finds that there have been serious lapses on the part of the Licence Authority- cum- C.M.O., Purnea as well as the Food Inspector, Purnea with regard to the present case.

From the materials brought on record by the petitioner himself in the supplementary affidavit, copy of PRN/F Licence No.
239/10-11 dated 04.10.2010 has been brought on record.

The same has been issued under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act') and Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Rules'), which prohibits any person to manufacture, sell, stock, distribute or exhibit for sale any article of food, including prepared food or ready to serve food, except under a licence.
The said licence is dated 04.10.2010 and seems to have been issued for the first time and is with regard to protein food, food supplements and proprietary food.
The fee for the same also seems to have been deposited through treasury challan on 01.10.2010.
4. In the background of the fact that the article in question namely, Zest Syrup is covered under the aforesaid Act and Rules and was seized from the shop of the petitioner on Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.2120 of 2015(7) dt.10-04-2019 02.09.2010, it is obvious that at the relevant point of time the petitioner did not possess any licence to deal with in such product.

However, unexplicably and indicating clear-cut collusion, the authorities concerned did not bother to take note of the basic requirement as to whether the petitioner was legally entitled or authorized to stock and sell such article.

Thus, no charge for not possessing a licence for dealing with such product and still the product being recovered from his shop and the authorities not charging him for the same under the relevant provisions for dealing with product without having a valid licence to do so, in the considered opinion of the Court, reflects grave irregularity.

Thus, this Court exercising power under Section 482 of the Code which is for securing the ends of justice and preventing the abuse of the process of the Court, deems it appropriate that the Principal Secretary of the Department of Health,
Government of Bihar, Patna be impleaded as opposite party no. 2.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Let necessary correction be made in the cause title of the application by learned counsel for the petitioner during course of the day.
5. Mr. Ashok Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the newly added opposite party no. 2.
The opposite party no. 2 shall look into the matter personally and file a Patna High Court CR.

MISC.
No.2120 of 2015(7) dt.10-04-2019 detailed counter affidavit on all aspects, including what has been observed in this order earlier.
He shall also specify as to what his Department proposes to do in the matter.

6. The matter be listed on 30th April, 2019 under the heading 'For Orders'.
7.
Mr. Ashok Kumar, learned APP shall communicate the order to the opposite party no. 2 for compliance.

(Ahsanuddin Amanullah, J) Anjani/-
